headline: High: Flowise can write shared files and egress broadly while Pipecat consumes shared-bus conversation state and calls third-party AI services, creating default risks of leakage and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while Pipecat exchanges conversation state over a shared bus. If Flowise outputs are bridged into Pipecat inputs, attacker-controlled content can become instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Flowise-generated text is forwarded into Pipecat prompts or tool inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the shared bus carries untrusted content as authoritative instructions, Pipecat may execute attacker-shaped directives.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Flowise outputs before handing them to Pipecat.
Insert a prompt-injection filter on the bridge.
Disable automatic forwarding between the agents.
Require human review for any Flowise text that becomes Pipecat input.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and has broad network egress; Pipecat handles text, audio/video, conversation state, and sends data to many third-party STT/LLM/TTS services. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive chatflow content can flow into external APIs without a clear isolation boundary. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Flowise and Pipecat share a workspace, bus, or datastore, then chatflow content can cross between them.
IF Pipecat is configured with any third-party STT/LLM/TTS provider, shared content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Restrict Pipecat to local-only providers.
Remove sensitive fields from Flowise outputs before bridging.
Turn off shared-bus persistence for conversation state.
Review outbound destinations in both configs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has filesystem write access and server-datastore shared state across instances; Pipecat supports multiple instances over a shared bus. That creates overlapping mutable-state surfaces, though the profiles do not show unrestricted write to the same directory or git state. Uncertainty remains, so the safer medium severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same datastore, file tree, or bus namespace, state races can occur.
IF an orchestrator does not provide locking, concurrent updates may overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate storage namespaces.
Enable locking around shared writes.
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts.
Serialize updates through a single coordinator.
Audit for duplicate writers in deployment config.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces chatflow outputs and can call tools; Pipecat consumes conversation state and routes it through STT/LLM/TTS services. If Pipecat treats Flowise output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing speech. The profiles do not prove action-taking authority, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Flowise output as a prompt, transcript, or tool directive without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream services act on that propagated content, the cascade becomes user-visible.
mitigations: Add a verification step before Pipecat consumes Flowise output.
Constrain Flowise to structured outputs only.
Log and diff intermediate outputs for review.
Block direct action-taking from unverified text.
Use confidence thresholds before forwarding content.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials, while Pipecat processes audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics. If regulated or retention-sensitive data is routed from Flowise into Pipecat's third-party service stack, policy mismatches can arise. No residency or certification data is provided, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Flowise chatflows and forwarded to Pipecat providers, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention settings differ between the two stacks, deletion/export guarantees can diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before bridging.
Block regulated data from the pair unless approved.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document provider residency for Pipecat integrations.
Review secret-handling paths in Flowise.
